name: Diego Maradona
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1979 FIFA World Youth Championship at age 18, receiving the Golden Ball as tournament best player, and later won the 1986 FIFA World Cup at age 25.
early_history_summary: Maradona was spotted by a talent scout at age 8 and joined the Argentinos Juniors youth team Los Cebollitas. He made his professional debut at age 15 in October 1976, becoming the youngest player in Argentine Primera División history. By 1979, he was the top scorer in Argentine football and led Argentina to the World Youth Championship title.
family_context_summary: Born to a poor family in a shantytown in Villa Fiorito; father worked at a chemicals factory and mother was a homemaker. He was the first son after four daughters.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental football expertise or industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: prodigy talent, youth academy, mentor coach, poverty-driven
evidence_summary: Maradona's extraordinary football talent was recognized at age 8 when a youth coach could not believe a child could play so well. He joined Argentinos Juniors' youth system and made his professional debut at 15, the youngest in Argentine league history. By 18, he won the World Youth Championship Golden Ball. His family was poor—his father worked in a chemicals factory—and he grew up in a shantytown, but his prodigy-level talent earned him access to elite youth development and dedicated coaching from Francis Cornejo.

name: Ronnie Peterson
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1969 Formula Three Championship (both Swedish and European) at age 25, including the prestigious Monaco Grand Prix F3 support race, before making his Formula One debut in 1970 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Peterson developed his driving skills in karting from a young age in Örebro, Sweden, winning Swedish karting titles in 1963 and 1964. He co-designed a Formula Three car with his father and moved up to F3 racing, where his superb results attracted the Italian Tecno team, with whom he won the 1969 championship.
family_context_summary: Peterson was born in Örebro, Sweden. His father Bengt was a baker who co-designed a Formula Three car with him, showing practical mechanical support for his racing ambitions.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father Bengt co-designed a Formula Three car with Peterson and Sven Andersson, indicating hands-on mechanical involvement in his early racing career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: karting specialization, father mechanical support, European racing pipeline
evidence_summary: Peterson rose from karting in Örebro, Sweden, winning Swedish titles at 19-20, to Formula Three champion by 25. His father, a baker, co-designed an F3 car with him, providing practical mechanical support. The Italian Tecno team signed him based on his superb early results, connecting him to the European racing pipeline. No evidence of significant financial backing or elite family connections.

name: Isabel Allende
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Allende worked at the UN FAO and as a translator in her twenties, but her debut novel 'The House of the Spirits' was published in 1982 at age 40.

name: Svetlana Alexievich
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Alexievich graduated from Belarusian State University in 1972 and worked as a newspaper reporter, but her first book 'War's Unwomanly Face' was published in 1985 at age 37.

name: Evonne Goolagong Cawley
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1971 French Open at age 19 on debut, followed by the 1971 Wimbledon title, and went on to win multiple Australian Open titles (1974, 1975, 1976, 1977) and reach World No. 1 by 1976, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Goolagong grew up in an Aboriginal family in Barellan, NSW, where a local resident encouraged her to play tennis after seeing her peering through a fence. At 14, tennis school proprietor Vic Edwards spotted her, persuaded her parents to let her move to Sydney, and became her coach, guardian, and manager. She won her first Grand Slam at 19.
family_context_summary: Born to an Aboriginal (Wiradjuri) family in rural New South Wales; father was a sheep shearer and mother was a homemaker. She was the third of eight children and grew up during the Stolen Generations era, hiding from welfare officers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental tennis expertise or connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mentor coach, prodigy talent, Aboriginal adversity, tennis academy
evidence_summary: Goolagong's extraordinary tennis talent was spotted at 14 by Vic Edwards, who became her coach, guardian, and manager, moving her from rural Barellan to Sydney for elite training. She won her first Grand Slam at 19 (1971 French Open) and Wimbledon the same year. Growing up Aboriginal during the Stolen Generations era in a sheep-shearing family, her rise involved overcoming significant racial and economic disadvantage, with Edwards' mentorship providing the critical pipeline to professional tennis.

name: Jody Scheckter
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first Formula One Grand Prix at the 1974 Swedish Grand Prix at age 24, becoming the first South African to win an F1 race, and was a championship contender that same year.
early_history_summary: Scheckter rapidly ascended to Formula One after moving to Britain in early 1971. He made his F1 debut at the 1972 US Grand Prix with McLaren, where he ran as high as third before spinning. In 1973, he won the SCCA L&M Championship and raced in F1, though his reckless style drew criticism. Tyrrell signed him for 1974, where he matured and won his first Grand Prix.
family_context_summary: Born in East London, South Africa. Educated at Vincent Primary School and Port Rex Technical High School. Brother Ian Scheckter was also a racing driver who competed in F1.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental motorsport expertise, though brother Ian also raced in F1, suggesting possible family involvement in motorsport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: F1 team pipeline, rapid ascent, South African outsider, sibling racer
evidence_summary: Scheckter moved from South Africa to Britain at 20-21 and rapidly ascended to Formula One within a year, debuting with McLaren at 22. His natural driving talent was evident—he ran third in his first F1 race before spinning—but his early recklessness led to a ban. Tyrrell signed him for 1974, where he matured and won his first Grand Prix at 24. No evidence of significant family financial backing or motorsport connections, though his brother Ian also raced in F1.

name: Al Pacino
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Pacino was studying acting at HB Studio and the Actors Studio in his early twenties, working low-paying jobs. His first major theater role came in 1967 at age 27, Obie Award in 1968 at 28, Tony Award in 1969 at 29, and film stardom with The Godfather in 1972 at 32.

name: Claudia Schiffer
milestone_by_age_26: Achieved breakthrough as the face of Guess campaigns in 1989 at age 19, became Chanel's new face in 1990 at 20, and signed a record $6 million/year Revlon contract in 1992 at 22, becoming the highest-paid model in history—all well before 26.
early_history_summary: Schiffer was discovered at 17 in a Düsseldorf nightclub in 1987 by Michel Levaton, CEO of Metropolitan Models. She flew to Paris for a trial shoot, appeared on the cover of Elle, and was then selected for Guess campaigns in 1989 by Paul Marciano, which launched her to supermodel status. Karl Lagerfeld chose her as Chanel's new face in 1990.
family_context_summary: Born in Rheinberg, Germany, to father Heinz Schiffer, a lawyer, and mother Gudrun. She has two brothers and one sister. She originally aspired to become a lawyer and worked in her father's law firm.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a lawyer, and Schiffer worked in his law firm, but this is not directly relevant to her modeling career. No evidence of parental fashion or modeling industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: supermodel era, Guess campaign, Chanel face, physical distinctiveness, Paris fashion
evidence_summary: Schiffer was discovered at 17 in a Düsseldorf nightclub and quickly rose through Metropolitan Models to become the face of Guess in 1989 at 19, then Chanel in 1990. Her distinctive Bardot-like appearance and 5'11" frame made her naturally suited to high fashion. Her father was a lawyer providing middle-class stability, but no family fashion connections are documented. The late-1980s supermodel era was a massive structural wave she rode, with Karl Lagerfeld personally selecting her for Chanel.

name: Zinedine Zidane
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1998 FIFA World Cup with France at age 26, scoring two goals in the final, and received the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year the same year. Previously won Ligue 1 Player of the Year in 1996 and Serie A titles with Juventus.
early_history_summary: Zidane grew up in the tough La Castellane neighborhood of Marseille, the youngest of five children of Algerian immigrant parents. He started playing football at age 5 on the local plaza, joined US Saint-Henri at 10, and was spotted by AS Cannes scout Jean Varraud at 14. He made his professional debut with Cannes on May 18, 1989 at age 16, transferred to Bordeaux in 1992, and to Juventus in 1996.
family_context_summary: Born to Algerian immigrant parents in La Castellane, a tough neighborhood in Marseille. Father Smaïl worked as a warehouseman and security guard at a department store, often on night shifts. Mother was a housewife. Youngest of five siblings. The family lived reasonably comfortably by neighborhood standards.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental football expertise or industry connections. Father worked as a warehouseman and security guard.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cannes academy, French football pipeline, immigrant adversity, mentor coaches, street football
evidence_summary: Zidane grew up playing street football in the tough La Castellane neighborhood of Marseille, the son of Algerian immigrant parents. At 14, he was spotted by Cannes scout Jean Varraud at a French Football Federation camp and joined Cannes' training center, leaving his family. He made his professional debut at 16 and transferred to Bordeaux at 20, where coach Rolland Courbis became a father figure. His extraordinary technique was recognized early, but no family football connections or financial advantages are documented. The French football development pipeline and mentor coaches were critical to his rise.

name: Jules A. Hoffmann
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Hoffmann was completing his undergraduate studies at the University of Strasbourg in his early-to-mid twenties. His PhD was completed in 1969 at age 28, and his Nobel Prize came in 2011 at age 70.

name: Sudha Murty
milestone_by_age_26: Became the first female engineer hired at India's largest auto manufacturer, TATA Engineering and Locomotive Company (TELCO), in 1974 at age 23-24, after writing a postcard to the chairman challenging the 'men only' hiring policy.
early_history_summary: Murty was born in Shiggaon, Karnataka, India, to a surgeon father and schoolteacher mother. She completed a BEng in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from B.V.B. College and an MEng in Computer Science from the Indian Institute of Science. She then challenged TELCO's gender-discriminatory hiring policy by writing to the chairman, resulting in a special interview and immediate hiring as the company's first female engineer.
family_context_summary: Born to a Kannada-speaking family in Shiggaon, Karnataka. Father R.H. Kulkarni was a surgeon, mother Vimala was a schoolteacher. She was raised by parents and maternal grandparents. Her brother Shrinivas Kulkarni is a Caltech astrophysicist.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a surgeon and mother was a schoolteacher, providing an educated professional family environment. Brother Shrinivas Kulkarni is a prominent Caltech astrophysicist, suggesting a family culture of academic achievement.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IISc education, Tata Group, educated family, gender barrier-breaking
evidence_summary: Murty came from an educated professional family—her father was a surgeon, mother a teacher, and brother a Caltech astrophysicist. She earned an MEng in Computer Science from the elite Indian Institute of Science, then challenged TELCO's gender-discriminatory hiring by writing directly to the chairman, becoming the company's first female engineer at 23-24. The combination of elite education and family academic culture provided the foundation, while gender discrimination in Indian engineering created both a barrier and a catalyst for her breakthrough.

name: Nikola Jokić
milestone_by_age_26: Named the Adriatic (ABA) League regular season MVP in 2014-15 at age 20, averaging 15.4 points and league-leading 9.3 rebounds. Drafted 41st overall by the Denver Nuggets in the 2014 NBA Draft, made the NBA All-Rookie First Team in 2016, and became an NBA All-Star at 24, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Jokić grew up in a two-bedroom apartment in Sombor, Serbia, with his parents, grandmother, and two older brothers who were a decade older and played basketball. He played youth basketball for Vojvodina before signing with Mega Vizura in December 2012 at age 17. He developed rapidly, averaging 11.4 points in the Adriatic League in 2013-14, and was named ABA League MVP in 2014-15.
family_context_summary: Born in Sombor, Serbia to a family where his father was an agricultural engineer. He grew up in a two-bedroom apartment shared with his parents, grandmother, and two older brothers. His brothers Strahinja and Nemanja were a decade older and both played basketball.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an agricultural engineer. Two older brothers played basketball—Nemanja played college basketball for Detroit Mercy and C.W. Post and professionally in the Premier Basketball League. The brothers were friends with former NBA player Darko Miličić.
primary_early_advantage_tags: older basketball brothers, Serbian pipeline, Mega Basket development, daily street basketball
evidence_summary: Jokić grew up in a modest two-bedroom apartment in Sombor, Serbia, playing basketball daily with his two older brothers who were a decade older and played at college and professional levels. This intense early immersion gave him exceptional fundamentals and basketball IQ. He signed with Mega Basket at 17, where coach Dejan Milojević (a former ABA MVP) mentored him. By 20, he was named ABA League MVP. His father was an agricultural engineer—no significant financial advantages, but the sibling basketball environment was a powerful early advantage.
